title: Ruwanwelisaya
summary: Ruwanwelisaya, also called the Mahathupa, is a large stupa at Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka. King Dutugemunu began it and died before it was finished, so his brother Saddhatissa completed the work. The relic chamber is believed to hold relics of the Buddha. It now stands 103 m tall with a circumference of 290 m.

uncertainty.note: Start is around 140 BCE (astronomical -139) per ceylonhistory.com; the Sri Lanka Tourism page says only that it was built nearly 2500 years ago, which does not match, so confidence is probable. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: c. 140 BCE: construction begins under Dutugemunu

where.modern_name: Ruwanwelisaya, Anuradhapura, North Central Province, Sri Lanka
where.historical_name: Mahathupa (Ruwanweli Seya), Anuradhapura, under King Dutugemunu

importance.justification: Sri Lanka Tourism describes it as a great stupa believed to hold relics of the Buddha; the Central Cultural Fund lists it among the Anuradhapura dagobas that rank among the tallest ancient brick structures ever built.
